home.title: Rodrigo Rodriguez | Guitarist & Composer
home.desc: Guitarist and composer from Rio de Janeiro. The album Disrupção, a musical triad with Guilherme Salgueiro and Ygor Helbourn.
home.hero-sub: Guitar, voice and the code of the Rio scene. Two decades of partnership with Guilherme Salgueiro and Ygor Helbourn, distilled in Disrupção.
home.bio-1: A musical triad united for nearly two decades, Rodrigo Rodriguez, Guilherme Salgueiro and Ygor Helbourn bring their shared journey to life in the album “Disrupção”.
home.bio-2: Originating from Regra Zero and collaborating across various artistic fronts, including notable projects such as “Do Brasil with Moína Lima” and Rodrigo Quik's solo ventures in “Perdidos na Selva”, this collaboration reaches a new peak in the most recent album.
home.bio-3: The album that challenges expectations features Guilherme Salgueiro (bass; Monarco, Moacir Luz, Zé Catimba, Ana Costa, Ronaldo Barcelos, Dudu Nobre, Alcione) and Ygor Helbourn (drums; Marina Elali, Aki Kumar, Rodrigo Quik, Glaucus Linx). Yuri Helbourn also takes part in two tracks, playing bass in family synergy with his brother Ygor on drums. The album is produced and mixed by Cleidisleia, who also plays violin and fiddle.
home.bio-4: Rodrigo, Guilherme and Ygor, together for nearly 20 years, shaped their music through a shared journey in Regra Zero and in several of Rodrigo's artistic fronts, such as Do Brasil with Moína Lima (daughter of Taiguara) and Rodrigo Quik's solo projects (Perdidos na Selva). In “Disrupção” this collaboration reaches a new level, where the familiarity between the musicians translates into inventive bass lines and precise drumming that fit perfectly into Rodrigo Rodriguez's engaging compositions. They had not met for years, did not rehearse together, and recorded exactly the way they heard a demo recorded by Rodrigo and Cleidisleia days before.
home.bio-5: Produced in collaboration with Cleidisleia, who also plays violin and fiddle, “Disrupção” is a testament to Rodrigo Rodriguez's musical innovation. Cleidisleia, Guilherme Salgueiro, Yuri Helbourn and Ygor Helbourn add rich sound layers, and it is the track “Disrupção” that highlights the true essence of the relationship between Rodrigo's guitar and voice.

disrupcao.story-1: Rodrigo Rodriguez, Guilherme Salgueiro and Ygor Helbourn, a musical triad united for nearly two decades, bring their shared journey to the surface in the album “Disrupção”. Originating from Regra Zero and collaborating across several artistic fronts, including notable projects such as “Do Brasil with Moína Lima” and the solo ventures of Rodrigo Quik in “Perdidos na Selva”, this collaboration reaches a new peak in the most recent album.
disrupcao.story-2: Guitarist and vocalist Rodrigo Rodriguez is not alone in his latest musical endeavor. In “Disrupção”, the album that challenges expectations, the collaboration of nearly two decades with long-time companions Guilherme Salgueiro (bass; Monarco, Moacir Luz, Zé Catimba, Ana Costa, Ronaldo Barcelos, Dudu Nobre, Alcione) and Ygor Helbourn (drums; Marina Elali, Aki Kumar, Rodrigo Quik, Glaucus Linx) comes to life. Yuri Helbourn, Ygor's brother, also takes part in two tracks, and the album is produced and mixed by Cleidisleia, who also plays violin and fiddle.
disrupcao.story-3: Rodrigo, Guilherme and Ygor, together for nearly 20 years, shaped their music along a shared musical journey in Regra Zero and in several of Rodrigo's artistic fronts, such as Do Brasil with Moína Lima (daughter of Taiguara) and Rodrigo Quik's solo projects (Perdidos na Selva). In “Disrupção”, this collaboration reaches a new level, where the familiarity between the musicians translates into inventive bass lines and precise drumming that fit perfectly into Rodrigo Rodriguez's engaging compositions. They had not met for years, did not rehearse together, and recorded the way they heard a demo recorded by Rodrigo and Cleidisleia days before.
disrupcao.story-4: Produced in collaboration with Cleidisleia, who also plays violin and fiddle, “Disrupção” is a testament to Rodrigo Rodriguez's musical innovation. Cleidisleia, Guilherme Salgueiro, Yuri Helbourn and Ygor Helbourn add rich sound layers, and it is the track “Disrupção” that highlights the true essence of the relationship between Rodrigo's guitar and voice.

artist.celso.title: Celso Esteves | Rodrigo Rodriguez
artist.celso.bio: Celso Esteves, renowned Brazilian lyricist, stood out as a multifaceted artist, leaving an indelible mark on the music scene through his emotional and poetic lyrics. His passion for Maria Bethânia and Chico Buarque inspired memorable compositions, such as “Perdão” and “Ventania”. The perfect composing partner for Celso was Roberto Ferreira, whose collaboration deeply enriched the lyricist's creations.
artist.celso.collabs: Perdão, Ventania, Somos Sós, Degrau Por Degrau
artist.gui.title: Guilherme Salgueiro | Rodrigo Rodriguez
artist.gui.bio: Gui Salgueiro has played the night scene since he was 12 years old, starting his career at a festa junina in the neighborhood where he was born and raised: Vila Isabel. Since then he has played the most varied styles, from samba to rock, accompanying renowned artists such as Monarco, Moacir Luz, Zé Catimba, Ana Costa, Ronaldo Barcelos, Dudu Nobre and Alcione. He was part of Mart'nália's band and recorded the DVD Mart'nália em Samba with her.
artist.gui.collabs: Regra Zero, Disrupção, Linha do Tempo
artist.cleidisleia.title: Cleidisleia | Rodrigo Rodriguez
artist.cleidisleia.bio: Cleidisleia co-produced Disrupção with Rodrigo Rodriguez and played violin on Regra Zero. Her unique contribution brought a new sound dimension to the projects.
artist.cosenza.title: Rodrigo Cosenza | Rodrigo Rodriguez
artist.cosenza.bio: Rodrigo Cosenza is a guitarist and composer. He took part in bands of the Rio rock scene of the late 1990s and early 2000s, such as Gioconda and Columbia. He also played in the band Perdidos em Marte, which accompanied singer and composer Cíntia Luando.
artist.ygor.title: Ygor Helbourn | Rodrigo Rodriguez
artist.ygor.bio: Born into a musical universe, Ygor Helbourn is an eclectic drummer who stamps his personality on his musical projects. For over 10 years he has been part of the band Laranjeletric, which develops a black music work rooted in blues. He has taken part in several projects and accompanied numerous national and international artists such as Marina Elali, Aki Kumar, Rodrigo Quik and Glaucus Linx.
artist.ygor.collabs: Regra Zero, Disrupção, Linha do Tempo, A.M.E

disc.logx.title: LogX, Rodrigo Rodriguez
disc.logx.intro: Influenced by the Beatles, Dire Straits and Pink Floyd, LogX played the Vila Isabel rock scene of the late 1990s — houses like the Black Night sobrado and the bars of Rua Pereira Nunes — with Anderson Moura, Rodrigo Garcia, Felipe Moura, Rodrigo Cosenza and Rodrigo Rodriguez.
disc.logx.s1: Vila Isabel in the late 90s was a band factory. At the Black Night sobrado and the bars of Rua Pereira Nunes, rock rolled every week: Beatles, Dire Straits and Pink Floyd covers on one side, original songs on the other, and musicians' circles until sunrise.
disc.logx.s2: Passing by Rodrigo Garcia's house one day, Rodrigo Rodriguez heard a band playing and stopped to listen. He knew nobody there — he walked in and joined the circle anyway, and Rodrigo Cosenza soon gave him a job: compose Perguntas Idiotas Para Você with his lyrics. The song came out, the test was passed, and the band had its composer.
disc.logx.s3: Three recorded songs came out of the partnership, including Perguntas Idiotas Para Você and Último Corte — the surviving record of LogX.
disc.logx.s4: Felipe Moura had just learned to play bass. Rodriguez would pass him the notes and leave him free to create — that is how LogX sounded: fresh-off-the-stove technique, invention in place of habit.
artist.jehane.disc1desc: A completely self-written album: MPB, bossa nova, indie and world music with Arabic elements, derbak, oud, Rai. It closes with the French-language track “Je Ne Veux Plus”.
artist.jehane.q1: “Her work fuses POP, ROCK and oriental sonorities such as Rai, creating an authorial World Music work with electronic music timbres.”
artist.jehane.q2: “The songs are deeply moving... It is easy to understand the lyrics sung by Jehane with her captivating and hypnotic voice. How could she do it? Putting all her talents and emotions into a single album.”
artist.jehane.q2src: Niyi Fote, US music journalist, on “Exótica”

artist.rodrigogarcia.bio3: He played in the bands Onno, Ramirez, Polar, Anna Élle, Monotube and Indievíduos, and in cover bands of Brazilian Rock, Classic Rock and MPB.
artist.rodrigogarcia.bio4: He now plays in the band alongside Gui Salgueiro.

artist.bernardo.title: Bernardo Moura | Rodrigo Rodriguez
artist.bernardo.bio-1: Bernardo Moura is a guitarist and acoustic guitar player from Rio de Janeiro. A longtime companion of the Rio scene, he joined Rodrigo Rodriguez in the studio for the recording of Linha do Tempo.
artist.bernardo.bio-2: His acoustic guitar runs through “Se Você Acha”, one of the special guest moments of the album, adding a warm, timbral counterpoint to the electric guitars of the session.
artist.felipe.title: Felipe Moura | Rodrigo Rodriguez
artist.felipe.bio-1: Felipe Moura is a bass player from Rio de Janeiro. He joined the sessions of Linha do Tempo as one of the album's special guests.
artist.felipe.bio-2: His bass carries “O Que Você Era Pra Mim”, where his low end dialogues with the drums of Ygor Helbourn and the guitars of Rodrigo Rodriguez.
artist.felipe.bio-3: In the late 1990s he was the bass player of LogX, in the Vila Isabel rock scene — he had just learned the instrument when Rodriguez passed him the notes and left him free to create.
artist.lauro.title: Lauro Rodriguez | Rodrigo Rodriguez
artist.lauro.bio-1: Lauro Rodriguez is Rodrigo Rodriguez's brother, and the first one who taught him to play guitar and keyboard. The first chords of the whole catalog were learned at his side.
artist.lauro.bio-2: It was also Lauro who played “Sultans of Swing” to his brother, a door that opened straight into the guitar. He appears on the Roberto Ferreira & Celso Esteves album, in the family circle where the music began.
artist.wallace.title: Wallace Keyboards | Rodrigo Rodriguez
artist.wallace.bio-1: Wallace, known on stage as Wallace Keyboards, is a keyboard player from the Rio scene. Hammonds, Rhodes, synths: his palette covers the whole history of the keys.
artist.wallace.bio-2: He shares stages and studios with Rodrigo Rodriguez, coloring live arrangements and sessions with the harmonic glue that only a keyboardist brings to a trio of strings and skins.

artist.moina.title: Moína Lima | Rodrigo Rodriguez
artist.moina.bio-1: Moína Lima is a singer, composer and producer from Rio de Janeiro, daughter of the composer Taiguara. She leads Moína Produções Artísticas, an office dedicated to music production and to the memory of Brazilian song.
artist.moina.bio-2: With Rodrigo Rodriguez she recorded Do Brasil (2010), an album whose title track honors the song Do Brasil by Wanderley, a celebration of the Brazilian songbook. She also took part in the artistic production of Regra Zero, shaping the album's sound and arrangements.
artist.tajira.title: Tajira Kilima | Rodrigo Rodriguez
artist.tajira.bio-1: Tajira Kilima is a singer and performer, daughter of the composer Taiguara, alongside her sister Moína Lima. Music has been her language since childhood, on stage and in the studio.
artist.tajira.bio-2: She took part in the cultural production of Regra Zero, contributing to the project's artistic direction rather than performing on the record. Alongside her sister Moína Lima, she also helped shape the cultural side of Do Brasil, and performs in tributes to their father's work, including Taiguara: 80 Outubros.

bio.title: Biografia | Rodrigo Rodriguez
bio.desc: A musical biography of Rodrigo Rodriguez: the piano-playing grandmother and the flea-market violão, Salesianos, Michael de Paula, LogX, Regra Zero, Do Brasil, Linha do Tempo, Disrupção and what comes after.
bio.lead: Every house has a soundtrack. His had a piano, a violão brought home from the Feira de Acari, LPs spinning through cleaning days and louvores sung every afternoon. This is how a boy from Rocha Miranda became a composer.
bio.h2-roots: A grandmother at the piano, a violão from the flea market
bio.p-roots-1: His grandmother played piano and had one recurring sermon for his mother: look, these boys have to learn an instrument. Nobody in that house treated music as a hobby; it was a matter of inheritance, something to be passed on like a name.
bio.p-roots-2: His father, meanwhile, lived going to the Feira de Acari, coming home with trinkets of every kind. One day the trinket was a violão. He would gather the kids around it and almost, almost pull chords of Roberto Carlos songs out of the strings, and those almosts were the first music lessons. The grandmother who raised him sang every single afternoon: louvores from the sertão do Ceará, songs of the backlands carried into the suburbs of Rio. And his mother cleaned the house dancing, Sandra and Roberto Carlos on the turntable, housework performed as if it were a show.
bio.p-roots-3: Music did not arrive in that family. It was always there, in three generations at once: at the piano, at the flea market, at the mop.
bio.h2-brothers: Sultans of Swing, Bee Gees and the first chords
bio.p-brothers-1: His brother Lauro was the door. He showed him the first movements on the violão and on the keyboard, hand over hand, the way these things are actually transmitted. It was at their uncle Zé's house that Lauro played him Sultans of Swing for the first time, and uncle Zé himself who put Telegraph Road on soon after, the two tracks that opened the road to Dire Straits, The Beatles, Pink Floyd, Led Zeppelin, Rush, JJ Cale and Peter Gabriel, the whole canon entering the house one record at a time.
bio.p-brothers-2: His uncle Paulo lived in France for years and was a composer with several recorded tracks and radio performances, proof from up close that the composer's life was a real thing a family member could live. His uncle Ramon kept the Bee Gees spinning. The family passed records around the way other families pass photos.
bio.h2-twelve: Guitar, drums and Michael de Paula
bio.p-twelve-1: At twelve he picked up the violão for good. His father bought an electric guitar and a drum kit, the drums shared with his friend Alexandre, an arrangement that said everything about how music was lived in that circle: in pairs, in turns, together.
bio.p-twelve-2: Then, in school, came Michael de Paula. They formed a band, Rodrigo on keyboards and guitar, and Michael, more experienced, taught him how songs are actually built. He played the Salesianos school in Rocha Miranda many times and started writing instrumentals, his first originals, composed before he had ever sung a verse.
bio.h2-festivalda: Fest Valda, Morro da Urca, Circo Voador
bio.p-festivalda-1: In 1998 he entered the Fest Valda with a recorded cover of Sultans of Swing, a full-circle moment: the song his brother had shown him years earlier, now taken to a stage. He played the festival several times, in places like the Morro da Urca and the Circo Voador, and the instrumentals kept coming.
bio.h2-logx: Vila Isabel, two Rodrigos and one test
bio.p-logx-1: After moving from Rocha Miranda, he met Rodrigo Garcia and Rodrigo Cosenza in Vila Isabel in 1998. They ordered a song from him, as a test. He came back with Perguntas Idiotas Para Você with Cozensa's lyrics, and the test was passed. Two years of shows followed, during which Cosenza introduced Rodrigo to the poet.
bio.p-logx-2: With Garcia and Cozenza he recorded As Melhores Coisas da Vida, shaped by the LogX sound, thinking that was where it ended. It was not.
bio.h2-zero: Regra Zero, Canecão and Do Brasil
bio.p-zero-1: Then came the idea of his own band. He founded Regra Zero, which carried his songs around Rio's stages, including the Canecão. It was there he met Moína and Tajira Kilima, and that meeting became Do Brasil with Moína, released in 2010, a project celebrating Brazilian song.
bio.p-zero-2: Feeling the pull of another album, he left for Linha do Tempo: a polished record, where technology and refined mixing work shaped every track.
bio.p-disrupcao-1: Soon after a first encounter with herb, Rodrigo let go of productivism and consumerism and wanted to record something that presented his voice as it really was. That was where Disrupção began to emerge, recorded in 2019 with Cleidisleia, Ygor and Guilherme from the old Regra Zero circle, the triad back in the same room after years.
bio.p-disrupcao-2: At the album's launch in 2020 he met Jehane Saade, with whom he gave performances exploring her dance within the theme of Disrupção, the album becoming a stage piece as well as a record.
bio.p-mk-1: The myth had been dismantled at home long before. His father owned a bus, and helped with the production of Rock Estrela: music as work, gear in the luggage, a show that happens because someone drives, loads and sets it all up. Seeing it from the inside taught more than any mystique.
bio.h2-now: The next album, in the post-LLM era
bio.p-now-1: Today Rodrigo works on his next album, composed in the post-LLM era, a work about what remains human when machines learned to sing. On the horizon, at any moment now, the new work will be published.
bio.card-disc-sub: From LogX (1998) to Disrupção (2020), every release tells a chapter of this story.
bio.card-disrupcao-sub: Tracklist, credits and lyrics of the record where the triad returned.
bio.card-sw-sub: Twenty-five years of software architecture and General Bots, the open-source AI platform.
bio.h2-studio: Two tape recorders and a stack of reel-to-reels
bio.p-studio-1: The first recordings came from a setup as simple as it was ingenious: two cassette recorders, bouncing tracks from one to the other, layer after layer, until a song existed. That is where recording stopped being magic and became craft.
bio.p-studio-2: His father fed the obsession, buying old reel-to-reel recorders and bringing them home. On those machines Rodrigo taught himself sound engineering, trial by error, and that autodidact school later paid for itself: Regra Zero ended up recorded and mixed by the musician himself.
bio.p-brothers-3: And the singing came from both shores of the ocean. On voice, Sting and Michael Bolton. From Brazil, Legião Urbana, Barão Vermelho, Djavan, Tim Maia and Roupa Nova, the national songbook played side by side with the rock imports.
bio.p-mk-2: In 2000 came the encounters with the masters themselves: Mark Knopfler, crossed three times in Rio de Janeiro, plus Stanley Jordan and Mike Stern, close enough to see the gods of the guitar working up close. The lesson that stayed: the heroes are workers. Mastery is not magic; it is craft, repeated for decades, and it can be learned by anyone willing to put in the hours. The myth fell. The music remained.
